To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reduced dynamics of open quantum systems, which are described by the Schrodinger picture, is given by the time evolution of the density operator of the reduced system.

The time evolution of a system of N particles, initially in a pure correlated state, is equivalent to the time evolution of N independent particles, each in a reduced pure state, if the reduced state is chosen to be a pure state with the reduced density matrix equal to the reduced one of the initial state of the system.

the reduced dynamics of initially uncorrelated pure states of a quantum open system, when the environment is initially in its thermal equilibrium, is given by the Lindblad master equation with the standard Lindblad operators, while for initially correlated pure states the reduced dynamics is given by the same Lindblad equation with the modified Lindblad operators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the time evolution of the reduced density matrix of an open quantum system, which is initially in a correlated pure state.
the development of an effective method to deal with the reduced dynamics of open many-body quantum systems.
a new method for the reduced time evolution of initially correlated pure states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the time evolution of the density operator of the reduced system is not always given by a completely positive map and the reduced time evolution of the reduced density operator is not always given in terms of an equation of the Lindblad type.
the reduced dynamics of an open system is not a Markovian process in general.
, if the reduced time evolution of initially uncorrelated pure states is considered, then the reduced dynamics is unitary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reduced time evolution can be obtained by solving the Schrodinger equations for the system and the environment, but in the case of initially correlated states the reduced time evolution is given by the Schrodinger evolution of the system alone.
the reduced dynamics is not a simple consequence of the initial conditions but depends on the initial correlations.
we have found a way to treat reduced dynamics by means of a Schrodinger equation, and that we have shown that the reduced dynamics is a unitary evolution in a larger Hilbert space.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reduced dynamics for initially correlated pure states can be obtained in a simple way by means of the reduced dynamics for uncorrelated pure states, and that the latter can be obtained by means of the dynamics of the total Hamiltonian.
, in contrast with previous approaches, the reduced dynamics of initially correlated states is described by a Schrodinger equation with an explicitly time-dependent Hamiltonian.
, in the case of initially correlated pure states, the reduced time evolution can be obtained by a unitary transformation of the initial pure state.
